newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs seen benefiting from yen's strength.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs seen benefiting from yen's strength.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to rise on Tuesday on the back of the yen's strength, which would help South Korean exports, brokers said.
"The yen's rise is likely to prompt buying by foreigners and institutions," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
The composite stock index closed 5.73 points lower at 773.51 on Monday.
Dealers said the yen was on the rise due to Japan's rising trade surplus. It currently hovers at around 112.50 to the dollar, against 113.48 last Friday.
Brokers said many blue chips faced further consolidation before resuming a climb.
They said semiconductor shares, including Samsung Electronics, would come under pressure in view of low chip prices in international markets.
Overall sentiment was backed by improving economic fundamentals, they said.
